column1: # IntelliJ IDEA Java code-style option inventory — the complete Java setting surface.
#     (`common` scope, and its nested `IndentOptions` as the `indent` scope)
#   scope           where the option lives in a code-style scheme XML:
#                   language-neutral, so its .editorconfig keys take the bare `ij_` domain)
#     editorconfig  no XML representation at all: an EditorConfig core property IntelliJ honors
#                   but stores outside the code-style scheme
#   value-kind      bool | int | string | wrap | brace | force-braces | package-table |
#                   (`wrap` / `brace` / `force-braces` are raw ints in XML and named tokens
#                    in .editorconfig, with a *different* table per kind)
#   editorconfig-key  the `.editorconfig` spelling, `-` when the option is XML-only.
#     lowercased, with the SPACE_WITHIN -> SPACES_WITHIN / SPACE_AROUND -> SPACES_AROUND
#     BRACE_STYLE -> block_brace_style, ...). Four settings surface under their universal
#     EditorConfig names instead (indent_size / tab_width / indent_style / max_line_length),
#     and two under the language-neutral `ij_` domain (ij_continuation_indent_size /
#     ij_smart_tabs). Java exposes only the SmartIndentOptionsEditor subset of
#     <indentOptions>; the rest of that scope is XML-only.
# `import::intellij`'s coverage test asserts every row here is captured by the model.
